transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-29
- Start: 16:00:00Z (08:00 PT / 11:00 ET)
- Duration: 53 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen, Derek Ruiz (Redwood); Sofia Patel, Liam O'Connor, Nadia Koval, Rashid Alvi (AuroraLink)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): AuroraLink exploring Redwood Private for inference workloads. Strong need for EU-region isolation, auditability, and integration with existing NGFW and on-prem peering. Next steps: runbook, SOC2 artifacts, pilot pricing.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh I'll hand it over to Sofia to, you know, say a quick intro on what you're aiming for
[00:06] Sofia: yeah thanks Maya, hi all. quick context — we run AuroraLink's ML platform, we have an inference layer internal that serves customers in europe and some in na. regulatory is pushing EU-first for certain verticals so we need private access for the model endpoints. we're evaluating options — hosted vs dedicated vs private — leaning private for now.
[00:28] Liam: yep and the big constraints are CIDR overlap with our corp vpcs, need for NGFW inspection on egress, and we have on-prem sites that need peering via transit gateway.
[00:40] Derek: got it, thanks. quick clarifying q — when you say private, are you picturing Redwood managed control plane with private dataplane in your VPC or full on-prem?
[00:48] Nadia: want the control plane to be Redwood hosted but we need the data path to terminate in our VPCs, yes. and keys managed in our KMS — we have HSM-backed KMS for sensitive workloads.
[00:59] Maya: perfect — that's our Private deployment pattern, the control plane remains SaaS but dataplane sits in your VPC. two quick follow-ups: primary region and whether you need multi-region active-active?
[01:10] Sofia: primary region is eu-west-1, possibly eu-central later. not planning active-active initial pilot, will want failover plan though.
[01:20] Rashid: from networking, we also need to confirm whether peering will be direct VPC peering or via transit gateway. our existing infra uses transit gateways for on-prem interconnects.
[01:29] Derek: okay transit gateway is fine — we support TGW peering and also privatelink-style endpoints depending on cloud. small caveat: for some clouds privatelink is the right pattern for private endpoints, for others we do VPC peering.
[01:43] Liam: is there any difference in latency or throughput between privatelink and peering? for inference at scale, we care about p99 latency.
[01:51] Derek: great q. peering tends to be slightly lower latency but lacks the service abstraction and endpoint ACLs. privatelink gives more control and integrates with AWS PrivateLink-type healthy endpoints, but you might see a small TCP overhead. overall for our token-level latency SLA we optimize kernels and runtime and both patterns meet p99 goals if the path is sized correctly.
[02:10] Maya: to add — we also do KV cache sticky routing and prefix-cache to reduce repeated token cost, that helps p99 when network is stable.
[02:19] Nadia: okay, pci and ISO teams will ask for audit trail — do you ship audit logs and do you support sending logs to our log collector?
[02:26] Derek: yes we have audit logs and can forward via secure syslog or S3 with SSE-KMS. control plane events are logged, and we can provide flow logs from the data plane; there might be a short retention tradeoff depending on plan.
[02:40] Sofia: quick note — we can't have any outbound egress to public internet for the EU workloads. everything must egress through our proxy/NGFW cluster. can Redwood support that?
[02:49] Maya: yes, our private dataplane can be placed in a subnet that only routes egress through your appliances — we have customers doing the same. Derek — maybe explain how we handle callbacks or model updates?
[02:59] Derek: sure. model artifacts and runtime images are pulled from our private registry; we can either mirror into your account or coordinate egress via your proxy. for callbacks, usually the control plane talks to the dataplane over mutual TLS inside the peered network, so no internet egress required for normal inference traffic.
[03:18] Liam: mirror sounds nice but there is operational overhead. how often do models update? some of our teams want frequent rolling updates.
[03:26] Derek: model rollout frequency is configurable — you can pin versions or allow auto updates. for pilot, we recommend pinning and doing canary promos.
[03:32] Sofia: okay. any gotchas on IP planning? our VPCs are pretty full, we have multiple /16s, but some teams overlap in /24 ranges.
[03:41] Maya: we usually ask for non-overlapping CIDRs for peering. if overlap exists we can use a transit-gateway-based NAT or customer edge NAT, but that's added complexity. we should get your CIDR ranges in the next step.
[03:53] Rashid: yeah we'll send ranges. also curious about route propagation and RTs — will Redwood require specific route tables per AZ?
[04:02] Derek: the dataplane uses subnets across AZs but you can have a single RT strategy, we provide recommended RT mappings in the runbook. for TGW we attach the subnet as a VPC attachment and have a managed ENI placed in your subnets.
[04:18] Nadia: about KMS — we need to ensure that envelope keys are customer-managed and that logs show KMS usage. is that supported?
[04:25] Derek: yes, SSE-KMS with customer-managed keys is supported; usage is auditable in CloudTrail. we can show sample CloudTrail events in the security pack.
[04:34] Sofia: great. competitor question — we ran a quick comparison vs OtherCloudAI and ModelServeCo. both offered private endpoints but were fuzzy on peering to TGW. what differentiates Redwood here?
[04:46] Maya: our distinction is runtime-level control and observability — token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and recommended batching/quantization profiles to save cost. also we run a unified experience for hosted, dedicated, and private so your ops runbook is consistent.
[05:01] Liam: ok sounds good. can you do a short pilot in eu-west-1 for a subset of traffic? we're thinking 100 rps steady with bursts and a dataset that is redacted.
[05:11] Maya: yes pilot is typical; we suggested 4 weeks earlier — Derek will prepare sizing & pilot SLOs.
[05:18] Derek: will do. one small technical note — if you require deep packet inspection in-line at NGFW, you may need to allow certain metadata traffic for model control (we'll document exact ports).
[05:30] Rashid: that's fine, we have a managed proxy cluster. will Redwood need us to open any public endpoints for health checks?
[05:38] Derek: no public checks are required for normal operations; only optional for metrics forwarding. most customers route metrics via a log collector or through a push gateway in their VPC.
[05:48] Sofia: ok, security also asked about data residency — logs and any persisted inference context must remain in eu-west-1. can you guarantee that?
[05:57] Maya: yes we can restrict persistence to the region for the private deployment. the control plane will be global but we can ensure no customer data leaves designated regions. we'll capture that in contract language.
[06:10] Nadia: can we see SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs?
[06:14] Maya: absolutely — we'll share the security pack after the call.
[06:19] Liam: network throughput — what's the recommended instance types for gpu carriers? we use a lot of large models and need predictable p95 throughput.
[06:28] Derek: we'll recommend a mix: A100-style GPUs for heavier models; for cost conscious workloads we offer quantized variants running on T4/RTX-class backends. the Dedicated dataplane in your VPC uses the same runtime. we'll provide perf numbers for the pilot.
[06:44] Sofia: one question about failover — if eu-west-1 goes down we need a documented failover to eu-central but it must be manual for compliance; can Redwood support manual failover?
[06:54] Derek: yes, we support manual and automated policies; we'll provide a canary rollback and manual runbook for your compliance sign-off.
[07:03] Rashid: last networking question — do you support AWS PrivateLink interface endpoints for the control plane to talk to our VPC?
[07:09] Derek: yes, in most clouds we can create interface endpoints. for AWS we typically use PrivateLink for control plane communications and keep the dataplane entirely inside your VPC.
[07:19] Speaker 1: [brief crosstalk]
[07:21] Maya: ok wrapping towards next steps — we'll compile a runbook, pricing for pilot, and the SOC2 pack. anything else from AuroraLink?
[07:29] Sofia: please include an explicit egress diagram showing how the NGFW sits in line and where model updates download from.
[07:36] Maya: will do. Derek — can you prepare a short 30-min deep-dive for Rashid and network folks next week?
[07:42] Derek: yes can do, propose Jan 6 or Jan 5 — whichever works for them.
[07:47] Liam: Jan 6 works.
[07:50] Nadia: one more compliance nuance — our legal wants explicit language about log access and retention for at least 2 years.
[07:58] Maya: we'll include retention options and will mark the default and extended retention tiers.
[08:03] Sofia: great. thanks everyone, that was helpful. we'll share the CIDRs and the compliance calendar after this meeting.
[08:11] Maya: excellent. thanks all, we'll follow up with the checklist and runbook.
